key_insight: In urban Haiti, moderate-to-severe depressive symptoms were linked to a higher prevalence of cardiovascular disease, with the association appearing stronger in women.
clinical_relevance: Depression screening may be an important addition to cardiovascular prevention efforts in low-resource settings where both conditions are common.
method: Cross-sectional analysis of 2,995 adults enrolled in the Haiti Cardiovascular Disease Cohort.
Depressive symptoms were measured with the PHQ-9 and grouped as none-mild vs moderate-severe.
Prevalent cardiovascular disease was adjudicated using standard epidemiologic definitions; adjusted prevalence ratios were estimated with Poisson models.
evidence_signal: Participants with moderate-to-severe depressive symptoms had higher CVD prevalence, with an adjusted prevalence ratio of 1.36 (95% CI: 1.08–1.71) versus none-mild symptoms.
watch_item: Because the study is cross-sectional, it cannot determine whether depressive symptoms preceded cardiovascular disease or resulted from it.
paper_title: Depressive Symptoms and Prevalent Cardiovascular Disease: A Cross-Sectional Analysis in Port-au-Prince, Haiti
